title: LibreBase Market Intelligence & Competitive Positioning — August 2026
one_line_pitch: A new way of doing backend-as-a-service: agent-first, simple for humans and agents, yet secure. Open knowledge base and competitive intelligence platform — your data, your freedom to leave, your agents as first-class citizens.

north_stars.name: Open
north_stars.desc: Knowledge is free to find, attribute, and reuse. The core stays general-purpose; commercial layers sit on top.

north_stars.name: Lean
north_stars.desc: Dedicated instance ≤ 64 MB RSS north star (≤ 256 MB current gate). 1 container vs Supabase's 12.

north_stars.name: Fast
north_stars.desc: Supabase-class core-path latency/throughput vs Postgres 16 on equal hardware.

north_stars.name: Honest
north_stars.desc: No fake green status. No invented MB numbers. No 'as fast as Supabase' without evidence.

north_stars.name: Simple
north_stars.desc: Org → instance → project. Dedicated (1:1) and shared (1:N) both supported.

Supabase.description: Production-grade platform bundling Postgres, auth, storage, real-time into one portable system. Targets teams needing instant APIs and vector embeddings with strong security defaults.
Supabase.strengths: Fully bundled ecosystem (Auth + Storage) reduces initial setup time.
Supabase.weaknesses: Heavy resource consumption, hidden costs in Pro tier obscure true infrastructure spend, proprietary extensions → vendor lock-in.
Supabase.priceMotion: Freemium escalates quickly to vendor lock-in via proprietary extensions.

Neon.description: Serverless Postgres bundling auth, storage, AI features. Targets developers wanting low-memory backend without fake-green SaaS dashboards.
Neon.strengths: Per-project billing, instant scaling for variable load serverless workloads.
Neon.weaknesses: Lacks native agent-first features like embedded MCP integration out of the box, per-minute usage models lack predictable low-memory baselines.
Neon.priceMotion: Pay-per-use favors high-volume throughput but lacks predictable low-memory baselines.
